chunks: 5614 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim:

That Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام had him read the scroll of inheritance shares, which was dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and written in the handwriting of ʿAlī عليه السلام by his own hand, and I found in it:

“A man who leaves behind his daughter and his mother: the daughter has one-half, and the mother has one-sixth. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three shares belongs to the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share belongs to the mother. And I found in it: a man who leaves behind his daughter and his parents: the daughter has one-half, namely three shares, and the parents have...”
“For each one of them is one-sixth.”

“The estate is divided into five shares; whatever amounts to three belongs to the daughter, and whatever amounts to two shares belongs to the parents.” He said: And I read in it: “A man who leaves behind his daughter and his father: the daughter has one-half, and the father has one share. The estate is divided into four shares; whatever amounts to three belongs to the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share belongs to the father. And if he leaves behind two parents, a son, and a daughter, or sons and daughters, then the two parents have the two sixths, and whatever remains belongs to the sons and daughters...”
“For the male is the like of the share of two females.”

So if he leaves behind a son and two parents, then the two parents have the two sixths, and whatever remains belongs to the son. If he leaves behind a mother and a son, then the mother has one-sixth, and whatever remains belongs to the son. If he leaves behind a father and a son, then the father has one-sixth, and whatever remains belongs to the son. If he leaves behind a mother and sons and daughters, then the mother has one-sixth, and whatever remains belongs to the sons and daughters.
“For the male is the like of the share of two females.”
If he leaves behind his father and sons and daughters, then the father has one-sixth, and whatever remains belongs to the sons and daughters: “For the male is the like of the share of two females.”

key_terms.السُّدُسَانِ: the combined two sixths allotted to both parents
key_terms.السُّدُسُ: one-sixth of the estate as a fixed legal share
key_terms.النِّصْفُ: one-half of the estate as a fixed legal share
key_terms.صَحِيفَةَ الْفَرَائِضِ: the written scroll containing the laws of inheritance shares
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: the rule that a male child receives the share of two female children
key_terms.يُقْسَمُ الْمَالُ: the estate is apportioned into legal shares

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares of daughters, parents, and sons in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records inheritance rulings from the Ṣaḥīfah al-Farāʾiḍ, described as dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and written by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام. It details the fixed shares of daughters, parents, and children in several family combinations, including the principle that the male receives the share of two females among children.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5614 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Umar ibn Udhayna from Muhammad ibn Muslim that Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) had him read the "Scroll of Inheritance Shares," which was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) and written by Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) in his own handwriting.
In it, I found the following rulings:
"A man who leaves behind a daughter and his mother: the daughter receives half of the inheritance, and the mother receives one-sixth. The wealth is divided into four shares - three shares go to the daughter and one share to the mother.
If a man leaves behind a daughter and both of his parents: the daughter receives half (three shares), and each of the parents receives one-sixth. 
The wealth is divided into five shares - three shares for the daughter and two shares for the parents.
If a man leaves behind a daughter and his father: the daughter receives half, and the father receives one share. The wealth is divided into four shares - three shares for the daughter and one share for the father.
If a man leaves behind both parents, a son, and a daughter or sons and daughters, then the parents each receive one-sixth, and the remainder goes to the sons and daughters with the male receiving the share of two females.
If a man leaves behind a son and both parents, then each parent receives one-sixth of the inheritance, and the remainder belongs to the son.
If a man leaves behind a mother and a son, the mother receives one-sixth, and the remainder goes to the son.
If a man leaves behind a father and a son, the father receives one-sixth, and the remainder belongs to the son.
If a man leaves behind a mother along with sons and daughters, the mother receives one-sixth, and the remainder is divided among the sons and daughters, with the male receiving the share of two females.
If he leaves behind a father along with sons and daughters, the father receives one-sixth, and the remainder is divided among the sons and daughters, with the male receiving the share of two females."
